_: Biomes O' Plenty, from All the Mods 9's census (W4 R7, judged 2026-11-11). Named one by one, only the blocks that census saw as ground and judged, because a word a rule could read would take other mods' blocks with it, and because a file reaches a config that already holds detection's line where a changed rule does not. Brimstone's bricks, buds, clusters and fumaroles, the sandstones' cut, smooth and chiseled forms, slabs, stairs and walls, the flesh tendons and the glowing moss carpet were not judged and are left to the rules; white, black and orange sand and the null end stone already wear by detection.

Nether: brimstone is natural rock of the erupting inferno, the Nether's own ground, as basalt and blackstone are, and detection gave it stone by the stone in its name. Flesh: flesh and porous flesh are the floor of the visceral heap, the blocks the flesh family was made for (W4 T17), on a material no rule reads. Stone: white sandstone is natural rock of the tropics, as vanilla sandstone is, and the rules leave it out for the decorative word in its name.

Black and orange sandstone and dried salt, stone, natural rock as vanilla sandstone is; the glowing moss block, grass, a moss block as vanilla's is, and mossy black sand, grass, a turf judged by its living top; the null block, end, the ground of the end corruption, found only in the End. This census did not judge them, and they are named as 1.16.5's file and the 26.x files have them, so the editions match (W4 R14, 2026-11-13).

A slab or stair takes its full block's ruling (Xep, 2026-11-13: Can we make it so all slabs of blocks that wear, also wear, in their own like the full blocks do? and: Same with stairs as slabs; W4 R15). These are this mod's slabs and stairs whose full blocks a census of 1.20.1 judged, each named at its full block's family so it wears on its own texture as the full block does. A slab or stair of a block the census excluded, or never judged, is left as it was. Where an earlier note here leaves this mod's slabs and stairs to the rules, or to detection's family, the ones named below no longer are.
